national_raw_news.title: Asian Games: India wins five gold, two silver, two bronze medals today; Climbs to fourth place in medal tally 03 Oct 2026 | 9:25 PM 135
national_raw_news.content: India won five gold, two silver and two bronze medals at the Asian Games in Japan today. In Hockey, India thrashed Malaysia 5-1 to defend their men’s gold and the triumph also secured them a direct qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. For India, captain Harmanpreet Singh netted two goals while Jugraj, Hardik and Shilanand scored one goal each. In Men’s Cricket, India won the gold defeating arch-rivals Pakistan by 19 runs in the T20 final at Nisshin. Wrestler Aman Sehrawat clinched the men’s 57kg gold after edging out North Korea’s world champion Chong Song Han 11-7 in a fierce final. Kumkum Mohod won the individual gold medal in the women’s recurve archery event. In Golf, Pranavi Urs became the first Indian woman to win an Asian Games gold medal in the women’s individual title. India also bagged silver in the team event. Wrestler Antim Panghal sealed a silver medal in the women’s 53 kg category. Deepak Punia won bronze in the men’s 97kg freestyle wrestling event after defeating Mongolia’s Gankhuyag Ganbaatar. Archer Neeraj Chauhan got bronze in the men’s individual recurve event. With these impressive performances, India has climbed to fourth position in the overall medal standings. The country’s medal tally has risen to 85, including 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals.

national_raw_news.title: Union Minister G. Kishan Reddy calls for coordinated, scientific planning based on people’s needs for Greater Hyderabad 2 hours ago 45
national_raw_news.content: Union Coal and Mines Minister G. Kishan Reddy has said that Greater Hyderabad cannot develop through slogans alone. He said it needs full coordination among officials and scientific plans based on people’s needs. Speaking to the media after chairing the Hyderabad District DISHA Committee meeting at CSIR-IICT, Tarnaka, he said the city should be planned as one unit, even though district and corporation boundaries differ. He asked the collectors of Hyderabad and Medchal-Malkajgiri, the GHMC and the three municipal commissioners in the Cyberabad area to work together. He will ask the Chief Secretary to arrange frequent joint reviews. The minister said 70 to 80 percent of Telangana’s revenue comes from Hyderabad and nearby districts. Yet GHMC and the Water Board are short of funds. He told officials to prepare detailed proposals to raise the city’s budget instead of relying on routine allocations. Big projects like Metro and Musi beautification are going on, he said. But the government must give top priority to daily civic problems like road repairs, drinking water, drain leaks, separate drains for sewage and rainwater, and street lights. Delayed bill payments must end so contractors come forward to work, he added. Kishan Reddy urged officials to transform government schools and anganwadi centres in slums. He asked state officials to send proper DPRs for central schemes. He promised to get funds sanctioned for Hyderabad and Telangana. Earlier, the meeting reviewed the Fatehnagar railway bridge, Ranigunj road widening, housing (480 houses per constituency), waste plants, shifting Bolakpur leather units, 39 STPs, and SHG loans.
